evidence.field: Oracle component account for 事; graphic history and bronze examples
evidence.text: The database describes oracle forms as hand (手) plus an unidentified component, depicting a hand holding something. It says the graphs 史、吏、事、使 later differentiated; in bronze forms an unbranched upper stroke is commonly assigned to 史 and a branched form to 吏/事. Bronze examples use 事 for duty, events, an office, and a command/serve verb. The identification of the held object is disputed: proposals include a flag, a document container, a brush, and hunting implements. These are source-reported analyses, not an established object identification.
evidence.kind: secondary paleographic database reporting inscription examples
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析, 又

evidence.field: Form sequence and interpretation for 事
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen form categories, without dating individual examples. Its note says ancient 史、事、使 were the same graph depicting a hand holding an object, and mentions hunting-tool and divination-tool identifications as proposals. The database terms page labels its pages All Rights Reserved; use this as linked evidence, not as an image asset.
evidence.title: 漢字「事」：字形演變

evidence.field: Attested senses and cited texts for 事
evidence.text: The database reports bronze-inscription uses for duty/office (麥鼎, 克鼎), event (琱生簋), office (小盂鼎), and command or service (小臣守簋). It also cites received texts for events/matters, undertaking, appointment, and serving, and cites the Qin Shuihudi daybook manuscript for 百事凶. These examples establish several uses but do not by themselves date the earliest occurrence of each sense or prove a single linear semantic development.
evidence.kind: secondary lexicographic database citing inscription and textual evidence
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 事

evidence.field: 史 comparisons, inscriptions, and proposed graphic history
evidence.text: The database says 史、吏、事、使 began as one graph and lists competing identifications for the object held by the hand. It reports oracle-bone 史 usages for an office, clan/person, matter, and ‘send’; in bronze it reports office usages and cases interchangeable with 事 and 使. It presents Wang Guowei's account of later differentiation into distinct small-seal graphs as a proposal, not a settled date. This evidence does not establish that 史 was a phonetic component in 事.
evidence.kind: secondary paleographic database reporting inscription examples and named analyses
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oracle-bone component analysis, 史

evidence.text: The entry lists senses including office/duty, occupation, matter, incident, serving, undertaking, administration, appointment, and use. It states that ancient 事、使、史、吏 were originally one graph and later differentiated. The listed senses are not a chronology.
evidence.title: 漢字「事」：基本資料

evidence.field: Shuowen analysis reported by an accessible character-specific page
evidence.text: Search results and the consulted 事 page identify the Shuowen account as 職也 and 从史，之省聲: ‘office/duty’; from 史 with an abbreviated 之 as phonetic. This is Xu Shen's later lexicographic analysis and is not independent proof of how the earlier graph was formed. The accessible result also reports two Guangyun fanqie readings, 側吏切 and 鉏吏切; these are not Baxter–Sagart reconstructions.
evidence.kind: dictionary reference reporting historical lexicographic analysis
evidence.title: 事 shì — 汉典

evidence.field: File description, identity, script scope, direct original, and reuse statement
evidence.text: The inspected description page identifies the file as a vector depiction of 事 in a Shuowen seal-script style and links the original SVG. This is a modern redraw, not a photograph or direct scan of an ancient artifact. The page states that the representation is public domain and that the creator released any copyright in the file. Its visible history records uploads in 2012 and 2022.
evidence.title: File:事-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK, Academia Sinica, Han Dian, and Commons pages. The exact ACC-s02204 description page and both Unicode Unihan endpoints returned internal errors.

search_audit.query: site:zdic.net/hans/事 職也 从史 之省聲 側吏 鉏吏; 事 Baxter Sagart *[m-s-]rəʔ-s 史 *s-rəʔ; Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang 事 字形 CC0; 史 事 吏 使 甲骨文 金文 分化 事 睡虎地 秦簡 事 百事兇
search_audit.outcome: The Xiaoxuetang home page opened but the character-specific query could not be accessed. A relevant Sinica PDF result timed out. Search results did not provide a directly inspectable primary Baxter–Sagart table or a usable character-specific Xiaoxuetang glyph record.

gaps: The exact earliest attested instance and archaeological date of 事 were not established: the consulted databases label oracle-bone and bronze categories, but the accessible records do not date a first specimen.

The held object's original identity and name remain disputed. Since no independent evidence establishes the object's name or pronunciation, a whole-graph loan from that object's name is not demonstrated.

The Shuowen account 从史，之省聲 conflicts with the paleographic description of the related graphs as later differentiated from an earlier shared graph. The available sources do not establish a phonetic role for 史 in the ancient form of 事.

The local primary reading rows supplied in the task give Unihan kMandarin 事 shì and 史 shǐ, and Baxter–Sagart 2014 MC dzriH / OC *[m-s-]rəʔ-s for 事 and MC sriX / OC *s-rəʔ for 史. These are local structured data, not externally verified rows in this run. The official Unicode character pages failed to open, and no externally inspected primary Baxter–Sagart source was found. Current readings do not prove ancient phonetic function.

No source established a semantic chronology for all senses. The CUHK page supplies cited examples, including bronze inscriptions and the Shuihudi Qin manuscript, but not a complete dating argument for semantic extensions.

The relevant Academia Sinica character-specific page says All Rights Reserved, so it is not proposed as an image. The Xiaoxuetang query record and rights notice could not be inspected sufficiently to select an image. The Commons candidate ACC-s02204.svg had a description-page access failure; it is not selected.
No repeatable local text extract is recommended: reuse permission for a wider database extract was not verified and a concise character-specific citation suffices.

items.period: Seal-script style, representing the Shuowen seal tradition; modern vector uploaded 2012, revised 2022
items.caption: Modern vector redraw of 事 in a Shuowen-style seal script. It illustrates the received seal form, not an ancient artifact or the disputed object in the oracle-bone graph.
items.alt: Black seal-script rendering of 事 centered on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons description identifies the graph and script style, provides the original SVG, and states public-domain reuse terms. It can illustrate the later seal-script form while making clear it is a modern redraw.
items.rights: Public domain, according to the file description; representation predates modern copyright and the creator released any rights in the file.

limitations.text: No selected image shows a directly photographed oracle-bone or bronze specimen. The only verified candidate is a modern vector of a received Shuowen-style seal form; it must not be captioned as an artifact photo.
